claims.text: A nuclear war could start by accident or miscalculation
claims.note: The paper lays out accidental and inadvertent routes to US-Russia nuclear war, noting that weather, a faulty chip, animals and misloaded training tapes have all been mistaken for attack indicators while both sides stay ready to launch on warning.

claims.text: Nuclear deterrence will eventually fail if it is relied on indefinitely
claims.note: It follows if a non-zero annual risk persists, but that risk can be lowered and the claim cannot be tested over its horizon.

claims.text: The annual risk of nuclear war between the great powers is small but adds up over time
claims.note: A fault-tree model estimates the annual probability of inadvertent US-Russia nuclear war at a mean of 0.02 (median 0.009, 90 percent range 0.0002-0.07), consistent with Hellman's roughly 1 percent a year, a small yearly risk that compounds over decades.

claims.text: Nuclear deterrence does not stop limited aggression below the nuclear threshold
claims.note: The Falklands, the 1973 war, the 1969 Sino-Soviet clashes and Kargil show nuclear-armed states attacked on a limited scale.

claims.text: US nuclear doctrine aims to prevail in a nuclear war rather than accept mutual assured destruction
claims.note: Declassified US guidance since Carter and Reagan speaks of prevailing and limiting damage, though leaders also say a nuclear war cannot be won.

claims.text: Limited nuclear use risks escalating to all-out nuclear war
claims.note: War games and stated Russian doctrine suggest escalation control is fragile, though no nuclear exchange has tested it.

claims.text: Dual-capable missiles blur the line between conventional and nuclear war and raise escalation risk
claims.note: Entanglement of conventional and nuclear systems is a widely recognised escalation pathway in Carnegie and RAND studies.

claims.text: China is rapidly expanding its nuclear arsenal
claims.note: SIPRI estimates China has about 620 warheads and is expanding faster than any other country, with hundreds of missiles loaded into new silo fields; even 1000 by 2030 would be about a quarter of the US or Russian stockpile.

claims.text: A new nuclear arms race is beginning between the US, Russia and China
claims.note: SIPRI says the post-Cold War decline in warhead numbers is likely to reverse as dismantlement slows and deployment of new weapons accelerates, with states 'fuelling arms-race dynamics'.

claims.text: US missile defences drive Russia and China to build up their nuclear forces
claims.note: Both cite US missile defence to justify new systems, but each also has other motives for its build-up.

claims.text: A full US-Russia nuclear exchange could cause a nuclear winter
claims.note: Climate models disagree on how much soot burning cities would loft; severe cooling is plausible but its size is disputed.

claims.text: The US, Russia and China are preparing to resume nuclear testing
claims.note: All three have expanded test-site activity and Russia revoked its CTBT ratification in 2023, but none has resumed explosive testing on the public record.

claims.text: A war with Iran would close the Strait of Hormuz and send oil prices soaring
claims.note: In the 2026 war Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, raising energy prices and creating what the paper calls an unprecedented global energy crisis.

claims.text: Russia and China will not fight to defend Iran
claims.note: During the 2026 war China and Russia backed Iran only diplomatically, vetoing a US-backed Security Council resolution on Hormuz, and did not fight.

claims.text: Killing Iran's leaders does not collapse the regime because its command is decentralized
claims.note: The war was launched on the bet that killing Iran's leadership would trigger an uprising and collapse; instead a younger, more hardline leadership took over, though the paper does not credit decentralised command.

claims.text: Air strikes alone cannot bring about regime change
claims.note: Studies of coercive air power find bombing rarely topples a regime without ground forces or an internal uprising.

claims.text: The US and its allies are running short of air-defense interceptors [2026]
claims.note: THAAD, Standard and Patriot interceptor stocks were heavily drawn down by the Iran wars and Ukraine, and production is slow to catch up.

claims.text: A long US war in the Middle East drains attention and munitions from deterring China
claims.note: Interceptor and munitions stocks shared across theatres are limited, and analysts and commanders warn of trade-offs with the Indo-Pacific.

claims.text: China and Russia are quietly aiding Iran's military without joining the war [2026]
claims.note: As of 2024, DoD finds China's help limited to a trilateral naval exercise with Russia, some training and China-based firms selling dual-use parts for Iran's missiles and drones, while Beijing is reluctant to deepen the relationship; it predates the 2026 war.

claims.text: The Islamic Republic will survive the US-Israeli war [2026]
claims.note: At the 8 April 2026 ceasefire Israel remained far from its principal aim, the collapse of the regime, and a new hardline leadership held power in Tehran.

claims.text: The US war with Iran is stuck in a stalemate [2026]
claims.note: By April 2026 the war had reached political deadlock, both sides claimed victory and the ceasefire came with no agreement on any US or Iranian point, but it ended in a truce rather than a static war.

claims.text: Iran's regime has had no elite or security defections despite war and sanctions [2026]
claims.note: Analysts report no significant defections through 2026, though this is hard to verify from outside.

claims.text: China keeps Iran's economy afloat by buying its oil despite US sanctions
claims.note: Tanker-tracking estimates put China's share of Iran's exported oil at around 90 percent, bought through intermediaries.

claims.text: US bases in the Gulf have become targets that expose host countries to attack
claims.note: Iran struck Al Udeid in 2025, and 2026 sources report Gulf bases and hosts hit again.

claims.text: The US will escalate the war with Iran after the November 2026 midterms
claims.note: A forecast made a week before the vote; carrier deployments make it plausible but it had not happened.

claims.text: Iran-aligned groups have widened the war to Saudi Arabia and the Red Sea [2026]
claims.note: Reported Houthi and Iraqi militia attacks on Saudi Arabia fit the claim, but how far Iran directs them is disputed.

claims.text: The Iran war is unpopular with the American public [2026]
claims.note: Polls cited in two 2026 sources show majorities opposed.

claims.text: The Doomsday Clock is closer to midnight than ever before [2026]
claims.note: The Bulletin set the Clock at 85 seconds to midnight in January 2026, 'the closest it has ever been to catastrophe'.

claims.text: The world is closer to a third world war than ever before
claims.note: Forecasters put great-power war well below even odds, and the Cuban missile crisis and 1983 were closer calls than anything on record since.

claims.text: Bible prophecy predicts a coming world war
claims.note: Whether Revelation foretells a future war is a matter of religious interpretation, not evidence.

claims.text: We are living in the last days foretold in the Bible
claims.note: A matter of faith with no testable content.

claims.text: The final conflicts of humanity will center on Jerusalem
claims.note: A prophetic reading, not a forecast that evidence can check.

claims.text: No one can know the date of the end times from signs like blood moons
claims.note: A theological position on date-setting.

claims.text: Iran has sponsored attacks through proxies that killed hundreds of Americans
claims.note: It includes 241 US service members in the 1983 Beirut bombing and about 600 deaths the Pentagon attributes to Iran-backed militias in Iraq.

claims.text: Iranian leaders have threatened to wipe Israel off the map
claims.note: Iranian leaders have repeatedly called for Israel's elimination, though the translation of the 2005 phrase is disputed.

claims.text: The US and China are in a second Cold War
claims.note: A common and useful analogy for the rivalry since about 2018, but the two economies are far more entwined than the US and Soviet ones were.

claims.text: Artificial intelligence makes the US-China rivalry more dangerous than the first Cold War
claims.note: RAND workshop experts agreed advanced AI could severely compromise strategic stability and that the resulting strategic arrangements could prove less stable than those of the US-Soviet Cold War, a forecast to 2040 rather than a finding about the US-China rivalry today.

claims.text: Today's geopolitical dangers are small compared with the 1930s, the 1940s or the worst of the Cold War
claims.note: No great-power war is under way and war deaths are far below those decades, but nuclear arsenals and arms control are in flux and the Doomsday Clock is at its closest.

claims.text: The US and China are in a military arms race in the Indo-Pacific
claims.note: DDIS: the US and China compete to develop advanced weapons, China is intensifying its build-up (the US less so), and the Pacific balance is shifting toward China.

claims.text: Arms races between great powers have historically led to war
claims.note: Studies find arms races raise the odds that disputes escalate, but many ended without war, the Cold War among them.

claims.text: History does not move in predictable cycles
claims.note: Clauset: interstate war onsets since 1823 fit a simple Poisson process with a constant hazard, meaning random, memoryless timing rather than cycles (for interstate war only).

claims.text: A civil war in the United States is highly unlikely
claims.note: Polarization is real but geographically mixed and political violence remains far below civil-war levels.

claims.text: Drones have made the war in Ukraine exceptionally lethal
claims.note: Ukrainian and Western estimates attribute most battlefield casualties on both sides to drones.

claims.text: North Korea's artillery and nuclear weapons deter any attack on it
claims.note: No state has attacked North Korea since 1953, and studies of a second Korean war project very heavy early losses in Seoul.

claims.text: North Korean missiles can reach the continental United States
claims.note: US intelligence states North Korea has successfully tested ICBMs capable of reaching the entire US homeland.

claims.text: North Korea has built a nuclear arsenal of dozens of warheads
claims.note: SIPRI estimates North Korea has possibly assembled around 60 warheads, with fissile material for at least 30 more and accelerating production.

claims.text: US homeland missile defence cannot reliably stop a North Korean ICBM
claims.note: Ground-based interceptor tests succeed only about half the time under scripted conditions against a single target.

claims.text: North Korean artillery could inflict mass casualties on Seoul in the first hours of a war
claims.note: Studies such as RAND's 2020 estimate tens of thousands of casualties in the first hour, though the video's millions-in-a-day figure is an older, higher estimate.

claims.text: North Korean troops have fought for Russia against Ukraine
claims.note: US intelligence describes North Korean troops participating in combat operations against Ukraine.

claims.text: North Korea funds its weapons programs through cybertheft
claims.note: US intelligence says North Korean cryptocurrency heists and other financial crimes net at least $1 billion a year to fund the regime's weapons programs.

claims.text: North Korea will not give up its nuclear weapons
claims.note: US intelligence judges North Korea strongly committed to expanding its nuclear arsenal and strategic weapons to solidify its deterrent, which offers no sign it will disarm.

claims.text: Most South Koreans support acquiring their own nuclear weapons
claims.note: Repeated polls since 2022 find roughly 70 percent support for an indigenous South Korean arsenal.

claims.text: The most likely future for the Korean peninsula is a frozen standoff without war
claims.note: The armistice has held for over seventy years and neither side gains from starting a war.

claims.text: Russia has moved to a war economy that is producing tanks at a high rate [2026]
claims.note: Russian defence spending is around 6-7 percent of GDP and open-source counts show large refurbishment and new T-90M output.

claims.text: Russia is stockpiling armour near Finland, Norway and the Baltic states [2026]
claims.note: DDIS reports Russia has deployed new army units along the Finnish border and behind the Baltic states, with far more troops expected after the war, but says the Ukraine war is delaying this build-up and does not mention armour stockpiles.

claims.text: A Russian armoured attack on the Baltic states or Finland would fail at heavy cost
claims.note: Against NATO air power it would likely take heavy losses, but wargames such as RAND's show Russia could still reach Baltic capitals quickly.

claims.text: Drones dominate defence, but taking ground still needs tanks protected by drones
claims.note: Ukraine shows drones blunt armour while combined drone and armour attacks have retaken some ground; the balance is still shifting.

claims.text: Russia is testing NATO with sabotage, drones and airspace violations
claims.note: US intelligence cites Russia's continued sabotage against US and European allies, such as the November 2025 railway explosion in Poland, and lists gray-zone tools including sabotage and military intimidation.

claims.text: Europe must build deterrence to stop Russia attacking its NATO neighbours
claims.note: EFIS credits steps taken by Estonia and Europe with making the Kremlin calculate carefully and says firm, steady preparedness is what truly deters Russia.

claims.text: World War 3 is much less likely than social media makes it seem
claims.note: Forecasters put great-power war in the next few years well below even odds, while feeds amplify alarming content.

claims.text: Great-power war has become rare since 1945 and remains unlikely in any given year
claims.note: Clauset: a constant-hazard model gives about a 43% chance of a WWII-sized war per century, small in any one year, but the long peace since 1945 is not statistically distinguishable from chance, so the 'has become rare' part is not shown.

claims.text: Nuclear deterrence has prevented a war between the great powers since 1945
claims.note: No great-power war since 1945 fits deterrence, but trade, institutions and US primacy also contributed, and it cannot be proven.

claims.text: Economic interdependence makes a US-China war less likely
claims.note: Trade raises the cost of war, but the evidence is mixed: dense trade did not prevent 1914, and US-China decoupling is reducing the tie.

claims.text: Missile defences would intercept a nuclear missile attack
claims.note: Missile defences are tested against a few missiles, succeed about half the time and cannot stop a large attack.

claims.text: Governments would hide a successful interception of a nuclear missile
claims.note: There is no evidence any nuclear-armed missile has been fired at a state, and a launch would be seen by many countries' early-warning satellites.

claims.text: The UN mediates conflicts before they escalate into a world war
claims.note: UN mediation has helped end some wars, but the Security Council is deadlocked where great powers are involved.

claims.text: Belief that a world war is inevitable is a danger in itself
claims.note: The case file says a general fatalism about an eventual European war, together with Russia's rise, encouraged an aggressive attitude among German leaders who favoured preventive war before 1914. It is a historical illustration, not a measured effect.

claims.text: The coming conflicts will be regional wars rather than one global war
claims.note: Conflict data show regional wars multiplying while forecasters keep a direct great-power war well below even odds in any given year, though this is a forecast.

claims.text: Russia lacks the military capacity to fight NATO
claims.note: Russia's conventional forces are far weaker than NATO's combined, but it could mount a limited attack on a frontline state and holds a large nuclear arsenal.

claims.text: NATO expansion provoked Russia's invasion of Ukraine
claims.note: NATO's 2008 promise to Ukraine was one grievance Moscow cited, but most historians weigh Russian imperial aims and Ukraine's turn to the EU at least as heavily, so a single provoking cause overstates it.

claims.text: A US or Israeli war with Iran could escalate into a wider world war
claims.note: The 2025 and 2026 rounds stayed regional and Russia and China kept out, so escalation to great-power war is possible but unlikely.

claims.text: The US and China are headed for war
claims.note: Metaculus's 629 forecasters put a US-China war (1,000 battle deaths in a year) at 8.7% before 2035; linked questions put it at 25% before 2050 and 0.5% by 2027.

claims.text: Taiwan will come under China's control peacefully as their economies grow together
claims.note: Polls in Taiwan show support for unification in single digits and a rising Taiwanese identity, so peaceful absorption looks unlikely on current trends.

claims.text: Nuclear weapons will not be used in today's wars
claims.note: US intelligence judges Russia will probably keep abiding by the norm against large-scale nuclear use unless the Ukraine war shifts significantly, so non-use is likely but conditional.

claims.text: The world is becoming more war-prone as US primacy fades
claims.note: Conflict datasets show state-based conflicts at their highest since the Second World War and US dominance has eroded, but most of the new fighting is not between great powers.

claims.text: The erosion of US security guarantees is pushing allies toward nuclear weapons
claims.note: The Bulletin reports that doubts about US extended deterrence have led European states to debate a Euro-deterrent or nuclear latency, and South Korea and Japan to hold similar debates.

claims.text: Economic pressure alone has not won a major war since the First World War
claims.note: Studies of blockades and sanctions find they rarely force a major power to give in without military defeat, though the answer depends on how strictly 'alone' is read.

claims.text: North Korea is unlikely to start a war it would lose
claims.note: Pyongyang has avoided full-scale war since 1953 and its doctrine stresses regime survival, though limited provocations continue.

claims.text: North Korea is selling large quantities of arms to Russia for its war in Ukraine
claims.note: EFIS: Russia has acquired an estimated 5-7 million artillery rounds from Iran and North Korea since 2023, with North Korean ammunition about half of Russian artillery fire in the second half of 2025.

claims.text: Russia is giving North Korea military technology in return for arms
claims.note: US intelligence says North Korean troops are gaining warfighting experience and military technology from Russia for taking part in the war.

claims.text: A small nuclear arsenal deters as well as a large one
claims.note: Minimum deterrence is a strategic judgment about what leaders fear; there is no test of how deterrence varies with arsenal size.

claims.text: The barriers to building nuclear weapons and missiles are falling
claims.note: Missile technology has clearly spread, as the Houthis show, but nuclear proliferation has stayed slow, with no new nuclear state since North Korea.

claims.text: More nuclear-armed states would make the world more dangerous
claims.note: Most scholars argue proliferation raises the odds of accident, theft and use, though a minority argue it spreads stability, and there is no clean test.

claims.text: A new US land-based ICBM is not worth its cost
claims.note: Whether the Sentinel missile is worth its rising cost is a budget and strategy judgment, not a testable fact.

claims.text: North Korea is more dangerous than ever
claims.note: North Korea's arsenal, missile range and Russian backing are at their peak, but greater capability is not the same as a greater intent to fight.

claims.text: The US faces an axis of Russia, China, Iran and North Korea acting together
claims.note: US intelligence finds selective cooperation among China, Russia, Iran and North Korea that adds to the threat, but calls it limited and mainly bilateral and says 'adversary alignment' overstates its depth.

claims.text: North Korea has abandoned no-first-use and threatens to use nuclear weapons first
claims.note: SIPRI notes North Korea's 2022 nuclear-use law allows pre-emptive nuclear use in the event of an attack, including by a non-nuclear-armed state.

claims.text: Russia's war in Ukraine has revived North Korea's economy
claims.note: Bank of Korea estimates show its fastest growth in years alongside Russian payments, though gains are concentrated in Pyongyang and rebound from a pandemic collapse.

claims.text: China is seeking to become the regional hegemon of Asia
claims.note: US intelligence says China aims to dominate its region and challenge Washington's leadership.

claims.text: Helping China grow rich created a US peer competitor
claims.note: Trade and WTO entry sped China's growth, which funds its military, though its rise owed most to its own reforms.

claims.text: The First World War was a preventive war started by Germany
claims.note: The Fischer school and others see German fear of a rising Russia as decisive, but many historians spread responsibility across several powers.

claims.text: Realist theory explains great-power behaviour better than liberal theories
claims.note: Clauset's finding that interstate war statistics look stationary supports realism's stationary null over liberal claims of a trend to peace, but it concerns aggregate war statistics, not great-power behaviour generally.

claims.text: World War 3 has already started
claims.note: No direct war between great powers is under way; the wars in Ukraine and with Iran remain regional.

claims.text: The US-Israeli strikes killed Iran's supreme leader at the start of the war [2026]
claims.note: The 2026 US intelligence threat assessment records the killing of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei on 28 February, the day the US-Israeli campaign began.

claims.text: Iran is no longer an existential threat to Israel
claims.note: Israeli strikes on Hezbollah and on Iran's air defences and missiles cut Iran's reach, but its remaining missiles and enriched uranium keep the threat open.

claims.text: The Iran war risks becoming a long war like Iraq
claims.note: Trump grew wary of a war lasting months with a costly ground operation, so the risk was real, but the fighting ended in a ceasefire after about forty days.

claims.text: Prehistoric hunter-gatherers rarely waged war
claims.note: Paleolithic evidence of warfare is sparse, but sites like Nataruk and Jebel Sahaba show group killing at or before the dawn of farming, and the record is thin both ways.

claims.text: War became common only after the rise of farming and settled societies
claims.note: Signs of warfare rise sharply with settlement and farming in many regions, though some earlier group violence existed.

claims.text: War is an innate part of human nature
claims.note: Humans show a capacity for both coalitional violence and long peace; whether war is innate depends on definitions.

claims.text: Pinker overstates prehistoric violent death rates by selecting violent samples
claims.note: Critics show his samples skew toward violent and post-farming sites, though his defenders note that lower-violence samples have their own gaps.

claims.text: Violence has declined over the long run of human history
claims.note: Homicide and per-capita war deaths fell over centuries in most datasets, though the statistical trend in war deaths is contested.

claims.text: A Chinese invasion of Taiwan is the most likely trigger of a world war
claims.note: Most analysts see Taiwan as the likeliest flashpoint for a US-China war, but an invasion itself remains unlikely in the near term.

claims.text: Russia would attack NATO if the US were drawn into a war with China
claims.note: DDIS says Russia's willingness to confront European NATO states would rise if the US shifted to the Indo-Pacific, and that a Taiwan war would reduce US ability to help Europe; heightened risk, not a predicted attack.

claims.text: Russia could launch a limited land grab against a Baltic NATO state
claims.note: European defence officials warn of this scenario, but Russia has not attacked NATO territory and NATO's forward forces raise the cost.

claims.text: The US would not defend the Baltic states under Trump
claims.note: Whether a US president would honour Article 5 is a question of intent that no public record settles.

claims.text: Arms-control treaties between the US and Russia have collapsed
claims.note: New START, the last bilateral US-Russia strategic arms treaty, expired in February 2026 with no successor, leaving US and Russian force levels unconstrained.

claims.text: Leaders of nuclear states increasingly threaten to use nuclear weapons in battle
claims.note: Russian and Pakistani officials have made such threats, but explicit threats of battlefield use remain confined to a few states.

claims.text: Space-based missile defence could start an arms race in space
claims.note: US intelligence judges that US space-architecture improvements, including plans for hundreds of missile-defence satellites, pose a security dilemma likely to push rivals toward new weapons and more aggressive strategies.

claims.text: Great powers now compete mainly through proxy wars, cyber attacks and information operations rather than direct fighting
claims.note: Rivalry between the US, Russia and China runs through arms to third parties, cyber intrusions and influence campaigns, while they avoid fighting each other directly.

claims.text: A limited nuclear exchange would escalate to all-out nuclear war
claims.note: FRI participants said a deliberate non-test detonation before 2030 would raise their probability of a 10-million-death catastrophe by 2045 4x (experts, from 5%) or 6.7x (superforecasters, from 1%), well short of certain escalation.

claims.text: The US no longer keeps tactical nuclear weapons in its arsenal
claims.note: The US still holds B61 gravity bombs, about a hundred of them deployed in Europe, and fielded the low-yield W76-2 warhead in 2020.

claims.text: A full nuclear war would kill most of humanity through nuclear winter
claims.note: One 2022 model estimates about five billion deaths from famine after a US-Russia war, but the severity of nuclear winter is disputed and other models find far less cooling.

claims.text: The number of armed conflicts worldwide is the highest since the Second World War [2024]
claims.note: UCDP counts 59 state-based conflicts in 2023 and 2024, then a record 65 in 2025, the highest since its data begin in 1946.

claims.text: World military spending has risen for a decade to a record high [2024]
claims.note: SIPRI: world military spending rose 2.9 percent in real terms to $2887 billion in 2025, the 11th consecutive annual rise and the highest level it has recorded, up 41 percent over 2016-25.

claims.text: Russia fired a new nuclear-capable intermediate-range ballistic missile at Ukraine [2024]
claims.note: US intelligence cites Russia's combat use of dual-capable intermediate-range ballistic missile systems in Ukraine.

claims.text: Military strikes on Iran increase its incentive to build a nuclear weapon
claims.note: Many analysts expect attacks to strengthen the case for a bomb inside Iran, but the same strikes destroy capacity and the regime's choice is not yet visible.

claims.text: Iran would answer a new US or Israeli attack with far heavier retaliation than in June 2025
claims.note: Unlike its limited response in June 2025, Iran answered the 2026 attack by closing the Strait of Hormuz, bringing the region to the brink of a wider war.

claims.text: If attacked, Iran would strike Gulf oil production rather than close the Strait of Hormuz
claims.note: When attacked in 2026, Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, and reopening it became the US condition for a truce.

claims.text: The US and Israel will strike Iran again [2026]
claims.note: After the June 2025 war, the US and Israel launched a wide-scale military operation against Iran on 28 February 2026 that lasted until 8 April.

claims.text: Iran is close to being able to build a nuclear weapon
claims.note: Before the 2025 strikes Iran could make weapons-grade uranium within weeks, but a deliverable weapon was judged months to a year or more away, and the strikes set it back.

claims.text: Gulf states pressed the US to seek a deal with Iran rather than war [2026]
claims.note: Oman hosted the talks and Saudi, Qatari and other Gulf leaders publicly urged a negotiated outcome to protect their economies.

claims.text: The Houthis would attack shipping and US forces if the US went to war with Iran
claims.note: The Houthis attacked Red Sea shipping and US ships in earlier rounds, but how fully they joined the 2026 war is not clear from the record at hand.

claims.text: The 2026 Iran war has already done enough damage to energy supply to cause a global recession
claims.note: Whether the 2026 oil shock tipped the world into recession is not established in the evidence at hand.

claims.text: Iran will have a nuclear weapon within a year if the US ends the 2026 war
claims.note: Strikes in 2025 and 2026 destroyed much of Iran's enrichment and weapons infrastructure; a bomb within a year is possible but not the expected case.

claims.text: Cheap attack drones can exhaust far costlier missile-defence interceptors
claims.note: Interceptors cost tens to hundreds of times more than Shahed-type drones and are produced far more slowly, a cost-exchange problem seen in Ukraine and the Gulf.

claims.text: Russia never negotiates an end to a war unless it has already won or lost
claims.note: Russia has accepted negotiated stalemates, such as the 1996 Khasavyurt accord in Chechnya and the 1940 Moscow Peace that ended the Winter War short of its aims.

claims.text: Russia will not stop until it reaches the Danube, the Carpathians, the Vistula and the Baltic
claims.note: That line runs through NATO territory, and forecasters put a Russian attack on NATO well under even odds; Russia's stated war aims centre on Ukraine.

claims.text: Air and naval power alone cannot force Iran to submit [2026]
claims.note: Six weeks of US-Israeli strikes failed to subdue Iran, which kept refusing US conditions until a ceasefire imposed largely by its closure of Hormuz.

claims.text: Using the Iran war to choke China's oil supply would lead to war with China
claims.note: China has supplied Iran but avoided any military clash with the US during the war, and forecasters see a US-China war as unlikely in the near term.

claims.text: Neither China nor Russia wants a war with the United States
claims.note: DDIS describes US-China preparations for a confrontation 'that neither side wants'; it says Russia sees itself in conflict with NATO and prepares for a possible war, without judging whether it wants one with the US.

claims.text: US forward bases near Iran and China can now be easily destroyed by precision missiles
claims.note: Precision strike makes fixed bases more vulnerable, but air defences and hardening mean US bases in the Gulf were hit, not wiped out, in 2025-26.

claims.text: The US war on Iran is driven by Israel and its lobby
claims.note: This Doha-based analysis says the war rested on Israeli-backed calculations and that Netanyahu long pushed for it, finding a receptive partner only in Trump; it shows Israeli influence, not a lobby driving US policy.

claims.text: President Trump could be removed from office over the Iran war
claims.note: Removal needs two-thirds of the Senate and no US president has ever been removed; the base rate is near zero.

claims.text: China is preparing its military to be able to take Taiwan by force
claims.note: US intelligence says the PLA keeps developing plans and capabilities to take Taiwan by force if directed and is making steady but uneven progress.

claims.text: A Chinese invasion of Taiwan would most likely fail at great cost to all sides
claims.note: Across 24 CSIS wargame runs of a 2026 invasion, the US, Taiwan and Japan usually defeated it, but at high cost: dozens of ships, hundreds of aircraft and tens of thousands of personnel lost, Taiwan's economy devastated and China's navy and amphibious force broken.

claims.text: A blockade of Taiwan is more likely than an invasion
claims.note: Most analysts and wargames judge coercion, quarantine or blockade more likely than a full amphibious assault, though both remain possible.

claims.text: China might use nuclear weapons if an invasion of Taiwan were failing
claims.note: DoD: Beijing increasingly seeks to use nuclear deterrence to limit adversary involvement in a conventional conflict while professing No First Use, which complicates signalling in a Taiwan conflict and raises the risk of unintended escalation.

claims.text: The US could not defend Taiwan without access to bases in Japan
claims.note: One of CSIS's four necessary conditions: without US bases in Japan, US fighter/attack aircraft cannot effectively take part in the war; Japan is 'the linchpin'.

claims.text: China's military has not fought a major war since 1979
claims.note: The PLA's last major war was the 1979 invasion of Vietnam, and it has made no contested amphibious landing since 1950.

claims.text: A US defence of Taiwan would likely cost aircraft carriers and hundreds of aircraft
claims.note: In CSIS's base scenario the US lost 168-372 aircraft and, in every iteration, two aircraft carriers plus 7-20 other major surface warships.

claims.text: Tribal and hunter-gatherer societies had far higher rates of violent death than modern states
claims.note: Ethnographic and archaeological data show high rates of violent death, though the samples are selective and the size of the gap is disputed.

claims.text: Homicide rates in Europe fell steeply from the Middle Ages to modern times
claims.note: Eisner's compilation of European records shows homicide falling from tens per 100,000 to about one.

claims.text: We are living in the most peaceful time in human history
claims.note: Per-capita violent death is low by historical standards, but battle deaths rose sharply in the 2020s with Ukraine, Gaza and Sudan.

claims.text: Trade makes people more valuable alive than dead and so reduces war
claims.note: Commercial-peace studies find a modest effect, but dense trade did not prevent 1914 or Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

claims.text: Strong central states reduce violence by removing the incentive to strike first
claims.note: Homicide fell as states consolidated and violence clusters in failed states, but correlation in timing is not proof of the mechanism.

claims.text: People overestimate violence because vivid news reports are easy to recall
claims.note: The availability bias is well established, but how much of public belief about violence it explains is less measured.

claims.text: European countries are rearming because they expect a war with Russia
claims.note: US intelligence says most European countries regard Russia as their greatest adversary and its invasion and gray-zone attacks have galvanised their defence focus; deterrence, not an expected war, is the stated aim.

claims.text: Britain faces an imminent all-out war
claims.note: The army chief urged preparation, not a date; forecasters put a direct NATO-Russia war within a few years well under even odds.

claims.text: An unintended incident could set off a third world war
claims.note: RAND sketches three plausible inadvertent incidents (NATO officials killed in Kyiv, a downed US surveillance plane, misread NATO moves) that could spiral to direct NATO-Russia war and potentially nuclear use, while noting most such events do not escalate.

claims.text: Putin did not intend to conquer all of Ukraine
claims.note: RAND describes Russia's 'expansive goals at the outset', including capturing Kyiv and 'denazifying' the government, scaled back to annexing four provinces only after failure.

claims.text: The US and Britain blocked a Russia-Ukraine peace deal in spring 2022
claims.note: Western leaders discouraged the Istanbul framework, but the talks also foundered on security guarantees and the Bucha revelations; Western veto as the decisive cause is disputed.

claims.text: Russia would use nuclear weapons if it faced defeat
claims.note: RAND's expert workshops find Russian nuclear escalation highly plausible and the most likely trigger a perception that battlefield losses threaten the regime, but stress Russia has a very high bar to battlefield use and may well avoid it even facing collapse.

claims.text: A Russian nuclear strike in Ukraine could draw NATO into a direct war with Russia
claims.note: US officials publicly threatened catastrophic conventional consequences for Russian nuclear use, a path that could bring NATO and Russia into direct combat, though it is only a possibility.

claims.text: A US-China war is a real possibility but can be avoided as the Cold War was
claims.note: Forecasters put a US-China war in the coming years well under even odds but not negligible, consistent with a real but avoidable risk.

claims.text: Crossing the Taiwan Strait makes an invasion of Taiwan very hard
claims.note: US intelligence says Chinese officials themselves recognise that an amphibious invasion of Taiwan would be extremely challenging.

claims.text: The US probably could not defeat China in a war over Taiwan
claims.note: CSIS's wargame found the US and Taiwan 'could successfully defend the island even under relatively pessimistic assumptions', contrary to many observers' impressions, though only if four conditions hold.

claims.text: Russia uses nuclear threats to deter Western support for Ukraine
claims.note: US intelligence records that since the invasion Russia has levied nuclear threats against the US and NATO and deployed nuclear weapons to Belarus.

claims.text: A world war is unlikely within the next six months
claims.note: Forecasters put the chance of a direct great-power war in any half-year in the low single digits even amid the current wars.

claims.text: Iran is the most powerful opponent the US has fought since the Second World War
claims.note: The US fought China directly in the Korean War, a far larger military, and Iran's economy and conventional forces are much smaller than a great power's.

claims.text: Control of the Strait of Hormuz will make Iran a fourth centre of world power
claims.note: Iran's economy is a small fraction of the US, Chinese or Indian economy and transit leverage does not create industrial or military power on that scale.

claims.text: The US military's costly high-tech weapons are ill-suited to wars against Iran or China
claims.note: Analysts widely warn of thin munitions stocks and vulnerable large ships against cheap drones and missiles, but US precision forces remain highly effective in many missions.

claims.text: Iran is more likely than not to get a nuclear weapon within a year
claims.note: FRI's 2024 experts and superforecasters gave Iran 25% and 30% chances of acquiring nuclear weapons by 2030, so not more likely than not within a year.

claims.text: The Iran war has shown US allies that America can be beaten
claims.note: Allied perceptions of US power after the 2026 war are not yet measured in any systematic way.

claims.text: Russia and Iran will lead a coalition invasion of Israel
claims.note: Russia keeps working ties with Israel and has shown no intent to attack it; Iran's strikes have been missile and proxy attacks, not an invasion with Russia.

claims.text: Iran's April 2024 missile and drone attack on Israel was almost entirely intercepted
claims.note: Israel, the US and allies reported intercepting nearly all of the roughly 300 drones and missiles, with minor damage at one air base.

claims.text: The world is more dangerous now than at any time since 1939
claims.note: Many experts and the Doomsday Clock rate current risk as very high, but most historians would rank the 1962 Cuban missile crisis as more dangerous.

claims.text: A single high-altitude nuclear blast could knock out the power grid across a large part of the US
claims.note: A high-altitude burst would cause an electromagnetic pulse that could damage grid equipment over a wide area, but how much would fail and for how long is disputed.

claims.text: France is deploying its nuclear warheads across Europe as a shield against Russia [2024]
claims.note: In 2024 Macron only offered to discuss a European dimension of French deterrence; he did not move submarine warheads across Europe.

claims.text: Global hostility toward Israel fulfils Bible prophecy of the end times
claims.note: A theological interpretation of current events.

claims.text: Russia runs influence operations on social media to divide Western publics
claims.note: DDIS reports Russian influence operations via online platforms and agents since 2022, aimed at sowing discord in Europe and weakening support for Ukraine.

claims.text: Russia cares more that Americans doubt their elections than about who wins
claims.note: Undermining trust was a documented aim, but the 2017 US intelligence assessment also found a clear Russian preference for one candidate in 2016.

claims.text: Russia uses information and cyber attacks to prepare the ground for military aggression
claims.note: DDIS says Russian hacking of transport and energy systems likely seeks access it could use to disable critical infrastructure immediately before or during a war against NATO.

claims.text: China uses economic co-optation and coercion to pursue its aims below the threshold of war
claims.note: DoD 2025 documents China using market access, trade, investment and supply chains to coerce opponents 'without resorting to military action', e.g. tariffs on Taiwan goods and import bans to push Guatemala to drop Taiwan.

claims.text: China is carrying out a historic military build-up
claims.note: DoD 2025 calls it 'China's historic military buildup': a large and growing nuclear, maritime, long-range strike, cyber and space arsenal that leaves the US homeland increasingly vulnerable.

claims.text: Integrating China into the world economy did not liberalize its politics
claims.note: Two decades after WTO entry China's one-party rule has tightened under Xi rather than liberalised.

claims.text: Authoritarian regimes are more brittle than democracies
claims.note: Personalist autocracies do collapse suddenly, but many one-party regimes have proved durable for decades.

claims.text: A direct war between great powers is likely within the next few years
claims.note: Metaculus's 'World War Three before 2050?' stands at 22% over about 24 years (3.3k forecasters), and the question conditional on AGI arriving puts World War III within five years of AGI at 4% (66 forecasters), both far under even odds for the next few years.

claims.text: A nuclear-armed state facing defeat would use its nuclear weapons before losing
claims.note: Nuclear powers have lost or retreated without using them (the US in Vietnam, the Soviets in Afghanistan, Israel's early 1973 setbacks, Russia in 2022).

claims.text: A great-power war would go nuclear before the US could mobilize its industry
claims.note: No war between nuclear powers has been fought, so whether escalation would outrun industrial mobilisation cannot be tested.

claims.text: A US seizure of Greenland would end NATO
claims.note: A counterfactual about an event that has not happened.

claims.text: Publicly releasing intelligence on Russia's build-up helped Ukraine survive the 2022 invasion
claims.note: The disclosures undercut Russian false-flag pretexts and rallied allies, but Ukraine's survival owed more to its forces and Russian planning failures.

claims.text: Europe is building up its own defence industry because it can no longer rely on the US
claims.note: EU rearmament plans since 2025 explicitly aim to reduce reliance on US weapons amid doubts about US commitment, though Russia is the main threat cited.

claims.text: The West is already at war with Russia through Ukraine
claims.note: The US and Europe arm and fund Ukraine in a proxy role, but are not belligerents fighting Russia directly.

claims.text: Russia has no tactical military reason to use nuclear weapons in Ukraine
claims.note: Dispersed forces and pervasive surveillance leave few massed targets where a tactical nuclear weapon would change the battle, a view many analysts share.

claims.text: NATO's nuclear arsenal deters Russia from using nuclear weapons
claims.note: Russia has not used nuclear weapons despite battlefield defeats, consistent with deterrence, though NATO has signalled a conventional rather than nuclear response.

claims.text: Predictions of a third world war have recurred continually since 1945
claims.note: Warnings of an imminent third world war appear in press and official statements from 1945 onward, and none has yet come true.

claims.text: A war between a rising power and a ruling power is the usual outcome of a power transition
claims.note: Hanania notes that adding Belfer's 14 candidate cases gives 19 wars in 30 transitions, and that since the mid-20th century only 1 of 7 (1 of 8 with US-China) ended in war. He argues the case selection is undefined, so war was common in older transitions but is not the usual outcome today.

claims.text: Wars between rising and ruling powers are usually triggered by a third party's provocation
claims.note: 1914 fits, but many power-transition wars were started directly by one of the rivals.

claims.text: China's economy would be half again larger than the US economy by 2024
claims.note: US nominal GDP was $10 trillion larger than China's in 2024, and at 2025 growth rates China would not pass the US in nominal GDP until 2041.

claims.text: China aims to be the world's leading power by 2049
claims.note: DoD 2025: China's national strategy is 'great rejuvenation' by 2049 with a 'world-class' military, and the report reads this as an ambition to displace the US as the most powerful nation.

claims.text: The post-1945 international order has kept the great powers from fighting each other
claims.note: There has been no direct great-power war since 1945, but nuclear deterrence and bipolarity are also credited and the order's role is debated.

claims.text: US intelligence assessed in 2025 that Iran was not building a nuclear weapon
claims.note: The ODNI's 2025 Annual Threat Assessment judged Iran was not building a nuclear weapon, while noting its enriched-uranium stockpile was at a record level.

claims.text: The US war on Iran was not about Iran's nuclear programme [2026]
claims.note: The paper says the war aimed to subdue Iran or topple its regime, yet the US terms put dismantling Iran's nuclear capabilities and ending enrichment first, so the nuclear programme was central but not the whole aim.

claims.text: China will invade Taiwan by 2027
claims.note: The US intelligence community assesses that Chinese leaders do not currently plan to invade Taiwan in 2027 and have no fixed timeline for unification.

claims.text: Chinese covert influence turned Taiwan's parliament pro-unification [2024]
claims.note: The opposition majority came from Taiwan's 2024 election; the KMT favours engagement with Beijing, not unification, and support for unification in Taiwan remains small.

claims.text: The United States is a declining power
claims.note: DDIS says China's growing influence has weakened the US position as the world's dominant power, leaving neither able to shape events alone; relative decline, not decline in absolute terms.

claims.text: A future world war would not resemble the Second World War
claims.note: A prediction about the form of a war that has not happened; recent wars mix drones, cyber and economic tools but remain heavily kinetic.

claims.text: Israel, not the US president, is directing US war policy on Iran
claims.note: Trump set and extended the deadlines and accepted a ceasefire to which Israel was not a party, while Israel claimed it would comply with whatever Washington asked.

claims.text: Great powers are locked in security competition that cannot be escaped
claims.note: Hanania quotes Mearsheimer and Walt on unavoidable competition (L101-114) but answers that great-power antagonism is a choice made by both sides, not 'the result of circumstances outside of human control'. Both positions are argued, not demonstrated.

claims.text: The US exit from the ABM Treaty and missile defences in Eastern Europe threatened Russia's nuclear deterrent
claims.note: Russia treated the sites as a threat and their launchers could in principle take offensive missiles, but the few interceptors there cannot blunt Russia's large arsenal.

claims.text: Russia complied with the nuclear arms treaties the US abandoned
claims.note: US intelligence says Russia has undermined arms-control agreements, suspended required New START data exchanges and deratified the CTBT, contradicting a record of compliance.

claims.text: Keeping great-power forces out of each other's neighbourhoods would reduce the risk of war
claims.note: Hanania argues that if restraint advocates pulled the US back from a militarized posture in East Asia there would be no Thucydides Trap, as when the US replaced France in Southeast Asia. This is a reasoned conjecture with no evidence that it lowers the risk of war.

claims.text: Russia was not isolated internationally after invading Ukraine
claims.note: Most UN members condemned the invasion, but most of the Global South declined to sanction Russia and kept trading with it.

claims.text: No large-scale amphibious invasion has been attempted since the Korean War
claims.note: Nothing since has matched Inchon's scale, though smaller opposed landings occurred, such as Cyprus in 1974 and the Falklands in 1982.

claims.text: The Taiwan Strait's weather and tides allow an invasion only a few times a year
claims.note: Monsoons and typhoons leave roughly two favourable windows, in spring and autumn, though they span weeks rather than single days.

claims.text: A Chinese attack on Taiwan would draw in Japan and other US allies
claims.note: US forces based in Japan make Japanese involvement likely in a full war, but allies' part in a blockade or limited conflict is uncertain.

claims.text: A war over Taiwan would cause a deeper global recession than the 2008 crisis
claims.note: Model estimates such as Bloomberg Economics' put a Taiwan war's hit to world output well above the 2008 crisis, though all such figures are scenario-based.

claims.text: Modern warfare favours the defence over the offence
claims.note: Ukraine shows defenders using drones and surveillance to stall offensives, but long-range missile and drone strikes still get through air defences.

claims.text: A well-prepared smaller country can deter or defeat a larger invader
claims.note: Ukraine stopped Russia's drive on Kyiv, but smaller states have often lost to larger invaders, and outcomes depend heavily on outside support.

claims.text: Sanctions on Russia have had no effect
claims.note: DDIS: Western sanctions exert intense pressure on Russia's economy, are a major factor in its reduced energy earnings, and have made military components more costly to obtain.

claims.text: Russia could be ready to attack NATO by 2030
claims.note: DDIS's timeline has Russia ready for a local war about six months after the Ukraine war stops or freezes, a regional war within two years and a large-scale war within five, conditional on NATO looking weak and failing to keep pace.

claims.text: Russia has no intention of attacking NATO
claims.note: EFIS states Russia has no intention of militarily attacking any NATO member in the coming year, but it limits this to the near term and ties it to continued deterrence.

claims.text: Russia has expanded its army and missile forces since 2022
claims.note: US intelligence says Russia's ground forces have grown despite wartime attrition and Russia fields advanced systems including hypersonic missiles.

claims.text: Missile and drone attacks now outmatch air defences
claims.note: Mass drone and missile salvos have saturated defences in Ukraine and the Gulf, but defences still intercept most incoming fire in many attacks.

claims.text: Air power alone cannot defeat the Houthis
claims.note: Years of Saudi, US and Israeli air campaigns degraded but did not stop Houthi missile and shipping attacks.

claims.text: US policy reversals make adversaries unwilling to strike deals with Washington
claims.note: Both rounds of US-Iran talks since 2025 ended with US or Israeli attacks, and Iran then refused talks without guarantees against renewed war; one case consistent with the claim.

claims.text: North Korea would lose a conventional war with the US and South Korea
claims.note: US and South Korean forces far outmatch the North's ageing conventional forces, though the North could inflict heavy damage first.

claims.text: Sanctions cannot stop North Korea because China keeps trading with it
claims.note: China accounts for the vast majority of North Korea's trade and has enforced UN sanctions loosely.

claims.text: China props up North Korea as a buffer against US forces
claims.note: Chinese strategists widely describe North Korea as a buffer, and Beijing keeps the 1961 alliance treaty in force.

claims.text: States that gave up nuclear weapons programmes were later attacked
claims.note: Libya and Ukraine were attacked after disarming, but Iraq had no weapons to give up, and South Africa and Kazakhstan were never attacked.

claims.text: South Korea's shrinking population will erode its military edge over North Korea
claims.note: South Korea's manpower pool is shrinking fast, but its economic and technological lead over the North remains vast.

claims.text: Markets and history show a major war follows a period of debt and wealth gaps
claims.note: Debt and inequality often precede internal turmoil, but historians find no reliable pattern linking them to great-power war; the big cycle rests on a selective reading of a few empires.

claims.text: The US faces a serious risk of civil war within the next decade
claims.note: Polarisation and political violence are rising, but forecasters and scholars put an organised US civil war far below one in three.

claims.text: Sanctions and capital wars usually come just before shooting wars
claims.note: The 1941 oil embargo preceded Pearl Harbor, but many heavy sanctions regimes, on Iran, Cuba or the USSR, never led to great-power war.

claims.text: The world is splitting into two blocs as before the world wars
claims.note: Russia, China, Iran and North Korea cooperate more and Western alliances have tightened, but much of the world, such as India and the Gulf states, stays non-aligned.

claims.text: The US no longer has a dominant military advantage over its rivals
claims.note: DDIS says China's military strength in the Western Pacific is already roughly on a par with the US and the balance will shift further its way; that is regional, not global.

claims.text: Using the dollar for sanctions pushes other countries away from holding dollars
claims.note: Central banks have shifted some reserves into gold since 2022, but the dollar's share of reserves has fallen only slowly.

claims.text: The US and China are already fighting trade, technology, influence and capital wars
claims.note: The WEF report describes trade disruption at its most severe in decades, sanctions and export controls spreading to AI, chips, quantum and rare earths, and pressure on countries not aligned with China or the US. It treats capital-flow conflict as a possible future front (L1372-L1373), not one under way.

claims.text: The world today resembles the eve of the First World War
claims.note: Multipolar rivalry and regional powder kegs echo 1914, but nuclear deterrence and the absence of mobilisation-driven war plans make the analogy loose.

claims.text: Today's conflicts resemble the imperial armed peace of small wars before 1914
claims.note: An interpretive framework for current conflicts, not a checkable fact.

claims.text: By a strict definition there have been many more than two world wars
claims.note: Under definitions like Hamilton and Herwig's (five or more major powers, fighting on two or more continents), several 17th- and 18th-century wars qualify.

claims.text: The US keeps the option of using nuclear weapons first
claims.note: SIPRI cites the 2018 US Nuclear Posture Review: the US would consider a nuclear response to 'significant non-nuclear strategic attacks', which is a first-use option.

claims.text: Today's conflicts are a global rebellion against US dominance
claims.note: UCDP says a widening array of states challenge norms upheld by US hegemony, but also that the US itself is turning against that order and that the conflicts are concentrated in a few countries.

claims.text: A renewed US war on Iran is imminent [2026]
claims.note: Polymarket's price that the US-Iran ceasefire holds falls from 83.5% through October 31 to 36% through November 30 and 29% through December 31, 2026, implying about a 70% chance of a new US strike on Iran before the year ends.

claims.text: A final US-Iran nuclear deal is unlikely [2026]
claims.note: As of April 2026, the US and Israeli demands (giving up 60% enriched material, ending enrichment, abandoning missiles) are seen by Iran as unrealistic, leaving a resumption of war possible.

claims.text: Iran will not give up its enriched uranium without lasting sanctions relief
claims.note: Iran demanded full lifting of sanctions, guarantees against future war and its right to enrich, and rejects handing over its 60% enriched material as unrealistic.

claims.text: The war with Iran will almost certainly escalate into a third world war
claims.note: The 2026 war ended in a Pakistan-brokered ceasefire after about forty days with no great-power fighting; Russia and China only vetoed a UN resolution.

claims.text: The United States will reinstate a military draft because of the war with Iran
claims.note: Automatic Selective Service registration is not a draft; induction needs a new act of Congress, and none has been proposed.

claims.text: The American empire will collapse within the next decade
claims.note: No base rate or model supports a dated collapse; the US remains the largest military and the issuer of the main reserve currency.

claims.text: NATO and Russia will fight directly over Odessa
claims.note: NATO governments have repeatedly ruled out sending combat forces to fight Russia in Ukraine, and forecasters put a direct NATO-Russia war well under even odds.

claims.text: The current conflicts are linked into one global war between two blocs
claims.note: The wars share some backers, such as Iranian drones and North Korean troops for Russia, but they are not one coordinated war, and China and Russia stayed out of the Iran war.

claims.text: The US attacked Iran to defend the dollar's reserve-currency status
claims.note: The paper gives the war's aims as subduing Iran or toppling its regime and does not mention the dollar.

claims.text: Conflict will break out in East Asia while the US is tied down in the Middle East
claims.note: No forecast or official threat assessment puts a war over Taiwan, Korea or the South China Sea in the next few years at anything near even odds.

claims.text: The US or Israel will strike Iran again by early 2027
claims.note: Polymarket implies about a 71% chance of a US air or missile strike on Iran before the end of 2026, so a US or Israeli strike by early 2027 is priced as likely.

claims.text: Iran will answer a new attack with escalation rather than restraint
claims.note: Iran met the 2026 attack with escalation (closing Hormuz) and refused to negotiate under fire; whether it would do so again after the ceasefire is untested.

claims.text: Economic blockades without a ground war rarely force major concessions
claims.note: Sanctions research finds economic pressure alone seldom wins major concessions, though the coding of some cases is disputed.

claims.text: Great powers are drawn into long wars because the first steps look easy
claims.note: Vietnam, Afghanistan and Iraq fit the pattern, but many interventions stayed limited; it is a tendency, not a rule.

claims.text: Iran will acquire a nuclear weapon
claims.note: 85% of surveyed strategists expect new nuclear states by 2036 and 66% of them name Iran (about 56% of all respondents), despite the 2025 strikes.

claims.text: The war with Iran is the first major US war since 1945 that began without majority public support
claims.note: Polling on the 2026 war is not independently checkable here; earlier wars such as Iraq in 2003 did start with majority support.

claims.text: The near-term risk of a Chinese invasion of Taiwan is low
claims.note: US intelligence expects Beijing to pursue unification short of conflict in 2026 and assesses no current plan to invade in 2027.

claims.text: China is trying to take Taiwan without fighting through coercion and influence
claims.note: US intelligence says Beijing will keep setting conditions for unification short of conflict and prefers to unify without force if possible.

claims.text: The risk of war over Taiwan rises after 2028 if Beijing's peaceful pressure fails
claims.note: A former DIA analyst quoted by CSIS argues China will not attack while peaceful unification seems viable but will once it judges force the only option; this matches the conditional mechanism but gives no 2028 date.

claims.text: China's military budget has grown faster than its economy for years
claims.note: China's estimated spending has risen 31 years running (62 percent over 2016-25) but held at 1.7 percent of GDP in 2025, the same as its 2016-24 average, so it has grown roughly in line with the economy, not faster.

claims.text: Wars in Ukraine and the Middle East have depleted US munitions needed to deter China
claims.note: Pentagon and think-tank reviews show interceptor and long-range munition stocks drawn down faster than they are replaced.

claims.text: Japan now treats a Chinese attack on Taiwan as a threat to its own security
claims.note: US intelligence notes Prime Minister Takaichi in November 2025 called a Chinese invasion of Taiwan a 'survival threatening situation' for Japan, a legal trigger for military action.

claims.text: China supplies dual-use goods that sustain Russia's and Iran's weapons production
claims.note: DoD 2025: China's state-owned defense firms supplied crucial dual-use components (semiconductors, radars, sensors) for Russia's weapons production; the report also cites sales of dual-use parts for Iran's missile and drone programs.

claims.text: Trump has put US arms sales to Taiwan on the negotiating table with China [2026]
claims.note: Based on reported summit readouts and leaks; the substance of the private talks is not public.

claims.text: The war with Iran has spread into a regional war across the Middle East [2026]
claims.note: Contemporary reports describe Iraqi militias, the Houthis and Gulf states drawn in, though no great power has joined the fighting.

claims.text: The United States has lost the war with Iran [2026]
claims.note: The campaign produced the opposite of its aims and Iran's closure of Hormuz 'imposed the ceasefire', but both sides claimed victory and Iran was also devastated, so 'lost' overstates it.

claims.text: Russia is winning the war in Ukraine [2026]
claims.note: US intelligence (March 2026) says Russia has kept the upper hand over the past year and is confident it will prevail on the battlefield.

claims.text: The Russian military is stronger today than at any time since the 1980s
claims.note: Russia's army is larger and battle-hardened, with higher arms output, but it has used up much of its Soviet equipment stock and is reconstituting rather than at a peak.

claims.text: Russia will attack a NATO country within the next few years
claims.note: Estonia's foreign intelligence (Feb 2026) assesses Russia has no intention of attacking Estonia or any NATO member in the coming year and expects the same next year, while warning capabilities will grow.

claims.text: Russia, China, Iran and Turkey are forming an axis that will dominate the Middle East
claims.note: Turkey is a NATO member at odds with Iran and Russia in Syria, and the others cooperate loosely without any alliance.

claims.text: Iran will drive the US military out of the Middle East
claims.note: US forces stayed in the Gulf through 2026, with more carrier groups sent in, and no withdrawal has been announced.

claims.text: Western economies will collapse under the energy shock of the war with Iran
claims.note: Past oil shocks caused recessions, not collapse, and benchmark prices eased during the war.

claims.text: A third world war is inevitable
claims.note: The Metaculus community gives a third world war only a 22% chance before 2050, the opposite of inevitable over the next quarter-century.

claims.text: The world today resembles the run-up to the Second World War
claims.note: A historical analogy, a way of framing events rather than a testable claim.

claims.text: Iran would not use a nuclear weapon against a US city
claims.note: Iran has no known nuclear weapon, and such an attack would invite devastating retaliation.

claims.text: US hostility with Iran grew out of the 1953 coup and US backing of the Shah
claims.note: The 1953 coup is a documented root of Iranian grievance, but the 1979 revolution, the hostage crisis and later proxy wars drive the hostility too.

claims.text: Fights over shipping chokepoints will draw more countries into the war
claims.note: Attacks on shipping have drawn in European and Asian navies before, as in the Red Sea in 2024, but mostly as escorts rather than combatants.

claims.text: The Saudi government will be overthrown within the next two years
claims.note: The Saudi monarchy has a long record of stability and there is no sign of an imminent revolt.

claims.text: Russia's military spending matches Europe's when adjusted for purchasing power
claims.note: IISS-style PPP estimates put Russia near Europe's nominal total, but that compares a PPP figure with a nominal one; Europe's own PPP spending is higher.

claims.text: Russia has suffered very heavy losses of troops and equipment in Ukraine
claims.note: UCDP: confirmed Russian battlefield deaths rose every year, from 42,000 in 2022 to 77,700 in 2025, against 14,000-24,000 a year for Ukraine, and these figures are expected to be revised upward.

claims.text: Russia would test NATO with a limited attack on one member rather than a full-scale war
claims.note: DDIS expects stronger Russian military provocations, possibly to test whether the US would come to Europe's aid, if Washington cast doubt on its commitment; provocations rather than an attack.

claims.text: A negotiated end to the US-Iran war is unlikely in the near term
claims.note: A ceasefire was negotiated in April 2026, but the paper calls the prospects of a permanent settlement hard to assess given the wide gap between the two sides' demands.

claims.text: The war with Iran has made a Chinese invasion of Taiwan less likely
claims.note: Some analysts read the war as a demonstration of US strike power and China's oil exposure; others argue depleted US munitions raise the risk. The net effect is uncertain.

claims.text: China would strike US air bases in Japan, Korea and Guam at the start of a Taiwan war
claims.note: Wargames such as CSIS's 2023 series assume early Chinese missile strikes on bases in Japan and Guam, but strikes on Korea, and how complete they would be, are less certain.

claims.text: Losing control of TikTok cut China's main channel for influencing American opinion
claims.note: The US ownership deal reduces one channel, but Chinese influence operations run across many platforms, so calling TikTok the main one overreaches.

claims.text: China's dependence on imported oil makes a Taiwan war harder to launch
claims.note: China imports most of its oil, but its large strategic stocks and Russian pipeline supply cover months of a blockade.

claims.text: Recent wars show that modern war bogs down even strong militaries
claims.note: Ukraine and Gaza became long wars of attrition, but short decisive campaigns such as Azerbaijan's in 2023 still happen.

claims.text: The US is waging a proxy war against Russia in Ukraine more intense than any Cold War proxy war
claims.note: Western arms and intelligence support for Ukraine has few Cold War parallels, but Soviet roles in Korea and Vietnam make 'more intense than any' a stretch, and 'proxy war' is a contested label.

claims.text: US wars in the Middle East and Ukraine weaken its ability to deter China
claims.note: Munitions and interceptors spent in Ukraine and the Middle East come from the same limited stocks needed in the Pacific, though most US naval and air power in Asia stays in place.

claims.text: The Ukraine war has driven Russia into closer alignment with China
claims.note: DDIS: Russia's dependence on China has deepened since the war, with about half its imports now from China against a quarter before, and military cooperation expected to continue after the war.

claims.text: Killing a regime's leaders rarely makes it surrender
claims.note: Studies of leadership decapitation find it seldom produces surrender or regime collapse on its own, but 'never works' overstates a mixed literature.

claims.text: The war in Ukraine will end in a frozen conflict rather than a negotiated peace
claims.note: Most forecasters expect any end to the fighting to be a ceasefire along the front line without a settled peace, but the war has not ended so the prediction is unresolved.

claims.text: World War 3 will start in 2028
claims.note: Metaculus forecasters give a world war 22% over the whole 2019-2050 window, so a start in the single year 2028 is far less likely than not.

claims.text: World War 3 will be triggered by false-flag attacks staged by globalists
claims.note: There is no evidence of any plan to stage false flags to start a world war; the claim rests on channelled visions.

claims.text: Psychic visions can predict when a world war will start
claims.note: Tests of psychic forecasting find no accuracy above chance, and this source's own timing for the war has already shifted.

claims.text: The war in Ukraine will spread to draw in Poland and Belarus
claims.note: After more than four years neither Poland nor Belarus has joined the fighting despite drone incursions, and forecasters put a direct Russia-NATO war in the next few years well under even odds.

claims.text: A third world war would be short
claims.note: CSIS warns a US-China war 'might not end after this initial phase but drag on for months or even years', since opening battles, even seemingly decisive ones, rarely end a war.

claims.text: A strong US and allied denial defence along the first island chain deters a Chinese attack
claims.note: Deterrence by denial is the mainstream strategy and has held so far, but whether it would deter China in a crisis is untested and depends on capabilities still being built.

claims.text: US-China relations are better than they have been in years [2026]
claims.note: A 2026 Trump-Xi summit eased the trade war and agreed a strategic-stability framing, but military competition, export controls and Taiwan tensions remain.

claims.text: Military-to-military communication reduces the risk of a US-China war by miscalculation
claims.note: Hotlines and incident agreements lower the odds that an accident escalates, though China has often cut these channels during crises.

claims.text: US allies in Asia are raising defence spending [2026]
claims.note: In 2025 Japan's spending rose 9.7 percent to its highest burden since 1958, Taiwan's rose 14 percent (largest since at least 1988, with a 5 percent of GDP goal by 2030) and South Korea's 2.6 percent.

claims.text: The US-Israeli war on Iran is aimed at weakening Russia and China
claims.note: The paper gives the war's aims as subduing Iran or toppling its regime and does not mention weakening Russia or China.

claims.text: Regime change in Iran is impossible without ground troops
claims.note: The air campaign failed to topple the regime and the US weighed a limited ground operation on Kharg Island, but the paper does not show that ground troops would succeed.

claims.text: A Chinese blockade of Taiwan would be a costly, high-risk operation rather than a low-cost option for China
claims.note: Wargames (CSIS and others) consistently find blockades bring casualties and escalation risk for China, though these are models, not observed outcomes.

claims.text: A Chinese blockade of Taiwan could escalate into a wider war involving the US
claims.note: US commitments under the Taiwan Relations Act and wargame results make escalation plausible, though its probability is uncertain.

claims.text: Taiwan cannot defend itself against China without US help
claims.note: China's defence budget and forces dwarf Taiwan's, and wargames find Taiwan's survival depends on US intervention.

claims.text: Taiwan's dependence on imported energy is its main weakness under a blockade
claims.note: Taiwan imports almost all of its energy and holds only days to weeks of LNG in reserve.

claims.text: Preparations such as stockpiles and resilient power could greatly improve Taiwan's ability to withstand a blockade
claims.note: Modelling shows larger fuel inventories and hardened power extend Taiwan's endurance, though this is untested in practice.

claims.text: An airlift could not sustain Taiwan's economy through a blockade
claims.note: Taiwan's population and bulk energy needs far exceed what Berlin's 1948 airlift carried; aircraft cannot move fuel at that scale.

claims.text: Wars and escalation are easier to start than to stop
claims.note: Many wars ran longer than planned, but many crises and limited clashes were de-escalated too.

claims.text: Defending Taiwan would cost the US more than it would gain
claims.note: CSIS documents the costs of defending Taiwan but explicitly 'does not take a position on whether the benefits of defending Taiwan outweigh the prospective costs'.

claims.text: The wars in Europe and the Middle East could merge with a Taiwan crisis into one world war
claims.note: A conceivable worst case, but the great powers have so far avoided fighting each other directly in either war.

claims.text: Iran does not pose a direct military threat to the US homeland
claims.note: Iran has no ICBM and no nuclear weapon; its threat is to US forces and partners in the region, not the US homeland.

claims.text: Trump's withdrawal from the Iran nuclear deal led Iran to expand its nuclear program
claims.note: IAEA reports show Iran complied until 2018-19, then enriched to 60% and grew its stockpile after the US withdrawal.

claims.text: The US will invade Cuba within the next few years
claims.note: Pressure, sanctions and an oil blockade are not an invasion, and nothing in the public record points to a planned invasion.

claims.text: Washington inflates foreign threats to justify defence budgets
claims.note: A claim about motives behind threat assessments that no measurement settles.

claims.text: Russia still holds to its maximalist war aims in Ukraine [2025]
claims.note: DDIS (Dec 2025) sees no sign Russia will make meaningful compromises: it will accept a ceasefire only if the vast majority of its demands are met, and officials hint at annexing Mykolaiv and Odesa too.

claims.text: Russia is likely to break any ceasefire in Ukraine
claims.note: A forecast of behaviour; Russia broke the Minsk ceasefires, but no general ceasefire has existed to test it.

claims.text: The last US-Russia nuclear arms treaty, New START, expires in 2026
claims.note: SIPRI records New START's expiry in February 2026.

claims.text: Russia has lowered its threshold for using nuclear weapons
claims.note: SIPRI records that Russia revised its doctrine in November 2024 to claim the right to use nuclear weapons against aggression by a non-nuclear state supported by a nuclear-armed state.

claims.text: Ukraine's fate after giving up its nuclear weapons will push other countries to seek them
claims.note: Public support for nuclear weapons has risen in South Korea and elsewhere, but no new state has begun a weapons program.

claims.text: The US commitment to defend European NATO allies has weakened under Trump
claims.note: The Munich Security Report cites Washington's gradual retreat, wavering support for Ukraine and threats over Greenland, and calls the US approach to European security volatile.

claims.text: Europe has the economic and industrial means to defend itself against Russia without US help
claims.note: Europe's economy dwarfs Russia's, but it lacks US enablers (intelligence, airlift, air defence) and needs years to replace them.

claims.text: China backs Russia because it sees the war in Ukraine as a proxy war against the US
claims.note: DDIS says China has a vested interest in the Russia-West conflict persisting because it diverts US attention from China, close to but not the same as seeing it as a proxy war.

claims.text: North Korea is gaining combat experience in Ukraine that it can use on the Korean peninsula
claims.note: US intelligence says North Korean troops are gaining valuable warfighting experience in Ukraine as a spillover of the war; its use on the peninsula is implied, not stated.

claims.text: Cheap drone swarms can overwhelm expensive air and missile defences
claims.note: In Ukraine, mass drone attacks saturate and exhaust air defences at far lower cost than the interceptors.

claims.text: Drones are replacing missiles and other conventional weapons in modern war
claims.note: Drones now cause most front-line casualties in Ukraine, but artillery, missiles and armour still play major roles.

claims.text: A drone incident between the two Koreas could escalate into a wider war
claims.note: Past incidents (the 2015 shelling, the 2022-24 drone incursions) did not escalate; the risk is real but small.

claims.text: North Korea is building a varied missile arsenal that can evade allied missile defences
claims.note: SIPRI reports North Korea unveiled and tested new systems in 2025, including the solid-fuelled Hwasong-20 ICBM and highly manoeuvrable medium-range systems designed to evade missile defences.

claims.text: Russia could stage a limited attack on a NATO state to test Article 5
claims.note: Intelligence services warn of this scenario, but no such attack has happened and forecasters put a Russia-NATO war in the next few years well under even odds.

claims.text: Russia's military has been hardened and modernised by the war in Ukraine
claims.note: US intelligence says Russia's ground forces have grown and its air and naval forces are arguably more capable than before the invasion, but does not attribute modernisation to combat experience.

claims.text: Europe's rearmament will not be ready in time for the period of greatest Russian threat
claims.note: Many European programs deliver in the 2030s, after the 2029-30 window that threat assessments flag.

claims.text: Rivals may exploit a US war in the Middle East to move on Taiwan or Ukraine
