contested.note: The 2025 and 2026 rounds stayed regional and Russia and China kept out, so escalation to great-power war is possible but unlikely.

contested.text: The US and China are headed for war
contested.note: Metaculus's 629 forecasters put a US-China war (1,000 battle deaths in a year) at 8.7% before 2035; linked questions put it at 25% before 2050 and 0.5% by 2027.

contested.text: Economic interdependence makes a US-China war less likely
contested.note: Trade raises the cost of war, but the evidence is mixed: dense trade did not prevent 1914, and US-China decoupling is reducing the tie.

contested.text: Iran is close to being able to build a nuclear weapon
contested.note: Before the 2025 strikes Iran could make weapons-grade uranium within weeks, but a deliverable weapon was judged months to a year or more away, and the strikes set it back.

contested.text: A direct war between great powers is likely within the next few years
contested.note: Metaculus's 'World War Three before 2050?' stands at 22% over about 24 years (3.3k forecasters), and the question conditional on AGI arriving puts World War III within five years of AGI at 4% (66 forecasters), both far under even odds for the next few years.

contested.text: Russia could be ready to attack NATO by 2030
contested.note: DDIS's timeline has Russia ready for a local war about six months after the Ukraine war stops or freezes, a regional war within two years and a large-scale war within five, conditional on NATO looking weak and failing to keep pace.

contested.text: US wars in the Middle East and Ukraine weaken its ability to deter China
contested.note: Munitions and interceptors spent in Ukraine and the Middle East come from the same limited stocks needed in the Pacific, though most US naval and air power in Asia stays in place.

contested.text: Israel, not the US president, is directing US war policy on Iran
contested.note: Trump set and extended the deadlines and accepted a ceasefire to which Israel was not a party, while Israel claimed it would comply with whatever Washington asked.

contested.text: The UN mediates conflicts before they escalate into a world war
contested.note: UN mediation has helped end some wars, but the Security Council is deadlocked where great powers are involved.

contested.text: Russia will attack a NATO country within the next few years
contested.note: Estonia's foreign intelligence (Feb 2026) assesses Russia has no intention of attacking Estonia or any NATO member in the coming year and expects the same next year, while warning capabilities will grow.

contested.text: Russia is winning the war in Ukraine [2026]
contested.note: US intelligence (March 2026) says Russia has kept the upper hand over the past year and is confident it will prevail on the battlefield.

contested.text: Russia would use nuclear weapons if it faced defeat
contested.note: RAND's expert workshops find Russian nuclear escalation highly plausible and the most likely trigger a perception that battlefield losses threaten the regime, but stress Russia has a very high bar to battlefield use and may well avoid it even facing collapse.

contested.text: An unintended incident could set off a third world war
contested.note: RAND sketches three plausible inadvertent incidents (NATO officials killed in Kyiv, a downed US surveillance plane, misread NATO moves) that could spiral to direct NATO-Russia war and potentially nuclear use, while noting most such events do not escalate.

contested.text: Wars in Ukraine and the Middle East have depleted US munitions needed to deter China
contested.note: Pentagon and think-tank reviews show interceptor and long-range munition stocks drawn down faster than they are replaced.

contested.text: The world today resembles the eve of the First World War
contested.note: Multipolar rivalry and regional powder kegs echo 1914, but nuclear deterrence and the absence of mobilisation-driven war plans make the analogy loose.

thinEvidence.text: NATO expansion provoked Russia's invasion of Ukraine
thinEvidence.note: NATO's 2008 promise to Ukraine was one grievance Moscow cited, but most historians weigh Russian imperial aims and Ukraine's turn to the EU at least as heavily, so a single provoking cause overstates it.

thinEvidence.text: The US and its allies are running short of air-defense interceptors [2026]
thinEvidence.note: THAAD, Standard and Patriot interceptor stocks were heavily drawn down by the Iran wars and Ukraine, and production is slow to catch up.

thinEvidence.text: Bible prophecy predicts a coming world war
thinEvidence.note: Whether Revelation foretells a future war is a matter of religious interpretation, not evidence.

thinEvidence.text: The barriers to building nuclear weapons and missiles are falling
thinEvidence.note: Missile technology has clearly spread, as the Houthis show, but nuclear proliferation has stayed slow, with no new nuclear state since North Korea.

thinEvidence.text: US intelligence assessed in 2025 that Iran was not building a nuclear weapon
thinEvidence.note: The ODNI's 2025 Annual Threat Assessment judged Iran was not building a nuclear weapon, while noting its enriched-uranium stockpile was at a record level.

thinEvidence.text: A long US war in the Middle East drains attention and munitions from deterring China
thinEvidence.note: Interceptor and munitions stocks shared across theatres are limited, and analysts and commanders warn of trade-offs with the Indo-Pacific.

thinEvidence.text: Most South Koreans support acquiring their own nuclear weapons
thinEvidence.note: Repeated polls since 2022 find roughly 70 percent support for an indigenous South Korean arsenal.

thinEvidence.text: North Korean artillery could inflict mass casualties on Seoul in the first hours of a war
thinEvidence.note: Studies such as RAND's 2020 estimate tens of thousands of casualties in the first hour, though the video's millions-in-a-day figure is an older, higher estimate.

thinEvidence.text: The US president alone can order a nuclear launch
thinEvidence.note: US command and control gives the president sole authority to order nuclear use without the consent of Congress or the cabinet.

thinEvidence.text: A US seizure of Greenland would end NATO
thinEvidence.note: A counterfactual about an event that has not happened.

thinEvidence.text: The US will escalate the war with Iran after the November 2026 midterms
thinEvidence.note: A forecast made a week before the vote; carrier deployments make it plausible but it had not happened.

thinEvidence.text: The 2026 Iran war has already done enough damage to energy supply to cause a global recession
thinEvidence.note: Whether the 2026 oil shock tipped the world into recession is not established in the evidence at hand.

thinEvidence.text: Air power alone cannot defeat the Houthis
thinEvidence.note: Years of Saudi, US and Israeli air campaigns degraded but did not stop Houthi missile and shipping attacks.

thinEvidence.text: An airlift could not sustain Taiwan's economy through a blockade
thinEvidence.note: Taiwan's population and bulk energy needs far exceed what Berlin's 1948 airlift carried; aircraft cannot move fuel at that scale.

thinEvidence.text: Announcing AI in nuclear command and control raises public perceptions of deterrence
thinEvidence.note: The evidence is a few survey experiments by one research group; it has not been widely replicated.

thinEvidence.text: Authoritarian regimes are more brittle than democracies
thinEvidence.note: Personalist autocracies do collapse suddenly, but many one-party regimes have proved durable for decades.

thinEvidence.text: The US and Britain blocked a Russia-Ukraine peace deal in spring 2022
thinEvidence.note: Western leaders discouraged the Istanbul framework, but the talks also foundered on security guarantees and the Bucha revelations; Western veto as the decisive cause is disputed.

thinEvidence.text: Britain faces an imminent all-out war
thinEvidence.note: The army chief urged preparation, not a date; forecasters put a direct NATO-Russia war within a few years well under even odds.

thinEvidence.text: The US cannot survive a global conflict if Russia and China are aligned against it
thinEvidence.note: The US and its allies outweigh Russia and China in economic output and naval power; the claim is a sweeping assertion.

thinEvidence.text: China has become more willing to risk escalation as its power has grown
thinEvidence.note: The evidence offered is war-game impressions; Beijing's real risk tolerance in a crisis is not publicly knowable.

thinEvidence.text: China is not racing the US to build artificial general intelligence
thinEvidence.note: Beijing's intentions are not public; its stated priorities stress applications and diffusion, but a covert programme cannot be ruled out.

thinEvidence.text: China is producing more AI researchers than the United States
thinEvidence.note: China graduates more STEM students and produces more top AI papers and undergraduate-trained AI researchers than the US, though many top researchers still work in the US.

thinEvidence.text: China props up North Korea as a buffer against US forces
thinEvidence.note: Chinese strategists widely describe North Korea as a buffer, and Beijing keeps the 1961 alliance treaty in force.

thinEvidence.text: A Chinese blockade of Taiwan could escalate into a wider war involving the US
thinEvidence.note: US commitments under the Taiwan Relations Act and wargame results make escalation plausible, though its probability is uncertain.

thinEvidence.text: A Chinese blockade of Taiwan would be a costly, high-risk operation rather than a low-cost option for China
thinEvidence.note: Wargames (CSIS and others) consistently find blockades bring casualties and escalation risk for China, though these are models, not observed outcomes.

thinEvidence.text: Chinese covert influence turned Taiwan's parliament pro-unification [2024]
thinEvidence.note: The opposition majority came from Taiwan's 2024 election; the KMT favours engagement with Beijing, not unification, and support for unification in Taiwan remains small.

thinEvidence.text: Chinese AI models trail the best American models by only months
thinEvidence.note: Benchmark trackers such as Epoch AI and Artificial Analysis estimate the gap at months rather than years.

thinEvidence.text: US chip export controls slow China's AI in the near term but speed up its own chip industry
thinEvidence.note: Controls have limited China's access to top chips while Beijing has poured money into domestic alternatives such as Huawei's Ascend.

thinEvidence.text: A civil war in the United States is highly unlikely
thinEvidence.note: Polarization is real but geographically mixed and political violence remains far below civil-war levels.

thinEvidence.text: Control of the Strait of Hormuz will make Iran a fourth centre of world power
thinEvidence.note: Iran's economy is a small fraction of the US, Chinese or Indian economy and transit leverage does not create industrial or military power on that scale.

thinEvidence.text: Countries go to war only when they disagree about who would win
thinEvidence.note: Disagreement about relative power is one recognised cause of war, but commitment problems and indivisible stakes also cause wars, so 'only' is too strong.

thinEvidence.text: Cutting-edge AI chips are harder for a state to produce than nuclear weapons
thinEvidence.note: Leading-edge chipmaking depends on a few firms and tools no state replicates alone, while several poor states have built bombs, though the cost comparison is rough.

thinEvidence.text: A drone incident between the two Koreas could escalate into a wider war
thinEvidence.note: Past incidents (the 2015 shelling, the 2022-24 drone incursions) did not escalate; the risk is real but small.

thinEvidence.text: Drones dominate defence, but taking ground still needs tanks protected by drones
thinEvidence.note: Ukraine shows drones blunt armour while combined drone and armour attacks have retaken some ground; the balance is still shifting.

thinEvidence.text: Drones will soon fight and choose targets fully autonomously without human involvement
thinEvidence.note: Autonomy is spreading fast in Ukraine, but most strike drones still need a human to pick the target and full autonomy at scale is not imminent.

thinEvidence.text: Economic blockades without a ground war rarely force major concessions
thinEvidence.note: Sanctions research finds economic pressure alone seldom wins major concessions, though the coding of some cases is disputed.

thinEvidence.text: Economic pressure alone has not won a major war since the First World War
thinEvidence.note: Studies of blockades and sanctions find they rarely force a major power to give in without military defeat, though the answer depends on how strictly 'alone' is read.

thinEvidence.text: Fights over shipping chokepoints will draw more countries into the war
thinEvidence.note: Attacks on shipping have drawn in European and Asian navies before, as in the Red Sea in 2024, but mostly as escorts rather than combatants.

thinEvidence.text: The final conflicts of humanity will center on Jerusalem
thinEvidence.note: A prophetic reading, not a forecast that evidence can check.

thinEvidence.text: A future world war would not resemble the Second World War
thinEvidence.note: A prediction about the form of a war that has not happened; recent wars mix drones, cyber and economic tools but remain heavily kinetic.

thinEvidence.text: The UN General Assembly has called for human control over AI in nuclear command and control
thinEvidence.note: The panel's diplomat co-authored the 2025 resolution; its exact wording on human control varied during negotiation.

thinEvidence.text: Global hostility toward Israel fulfils Bible prophecy of the end times
thinEvidence.note: A theological interpretation of current events.

thinEvidence.text: Governments would hide a successful interception of a nuclear missile
thinEvidence.note: There is no evidence any nuclear-armed missile has been fired at a state, and a launch would be seen by many countries' early-warning satellites.

thinEvidence.text: A great-power war would go nuclear before the US could mobilize its industry
thinEvidence.note: No war between nuclear powers has been fought, so whether escalation would outrun industrial mobilisation cannot be tested.

thinEvidence.text: The Gulf monarchies would collapse in a renewed war with Iran
thinEvidence.note: The Gulf monarchies have survived repeated Iranian and Houthi attacks on their infrastructure, and their reserves and security services are large.

thinEvidence.text: Helping China grow rich created a US peer competitor
thinEvidence.note: Trade and WTO entry sped China's growth, which funds its military, though its rise owed most to its own reforms.

thinEvidence.text: Homicide rates in Europe fell steeply from the Middle Ages to modern times
thinEvidence.note: Eisner's compilation of European records shows homicide falling from tens per 100,000 to about one.

thinEvidence.text: US hostility with Iran grew out of the 1953 coup and US backing of the Shah
thinEvidence.note: The 1953 coup is a documented root of Iranian grievance, but the 1979 revolution, the hostage crisis and later proxy wars drive the hostility too.

thinEvidence.text: The Houthis would attack shipping and US forces if the US went to war with Iran
thinEvidence.note: The Houthis attacked Red Sea shipping and US ships in earlier rounds, but how fully they joined the 2026 war is not clear from the record at hand.

thinEvidence.text: An ICBM cannot be recalled once launched
thinEvidence.note: US ICBMs have no recall or self-destruct mechanism after launch.

thinEvidence.text: Integrating China into the world economy did not liberalize its politics
thinEvidence.note: Two decades after WTO entry China's one-party rule has tightened under Xi rather than liberalised.

thinEvidence.text: Iran's April 2024 missile and drone attack on Israel was almost entirely intercepted
thinEvidence.note: Israel, the US and allies reported intercepting nearly all of the roughly 300 drones and missiles, with minor damage at one air base.

thinEvidence.text: Iran has sponsored attacks through proxies that killed hundreds of Americans
thinEvidence.note: It includes 241 US service members in the 1983 Beirut bombing and about 600 deaths the Pentagon attributes to Iran-backed militias in Iraq.

thinEvidence.text: Iran is no longer an existential threat to Israel
thinEvidence.note: Israeli strikes on Hezbollah and on Iran's air defences and missiles cut Iran's reach, but its remaining missiles and enriched uranium keep the threat open.

thinEvidence.text: Iran's military cannot stand up to the US military
thinEvidence.note: In conventional terms Iran is vastly outmatched, though it can impose costs asymmetrically through missiles, drones and shipping attacks.

thinEvidence.text: Iran is the most powerful opponent the US has fought since the Second World War
thinEvidence.note: The US fought China directly in the Korean War, a far larger military, and Iran's economy and conventional forces are much smaller than a great power's.

thinEvidence.text: Iran's regime has had no elite or security defections despite war and sanctions [2026]
thinEvidence.note: Analysts report no significant defections through 2026, though this is hard to verify from outside.

thinEvidence.text: The Iran war has shown US allies that America can be beaten
thinEvidence.note: Allied perceptions of US power after the 2026 war are not yet measured in any systematic way.

thinEvidence.text: The Iran war is unpopular with the American public [2026]
thinEvidence.note: Polls cited in two 2026 sources show majorities opposed.

thinEvidence.text: Iran will drive the US military out of the Middle East
thinEvidence.note: US forces stayed in the Gulf through 2026, with more carrier groups sent in, and no withdrawal has been announced.

thinEvidence.text: Iran will have a nuclear weapon within a year if the US ends the 2026 war
thinEvidence.note: Strikes in 2025 and 2026 destroyed much of Iran's enrichment and weapons infrastructure; a bomb within a year is possible but not the expected case.

thinEvidence.text: Iran would not use a nuclear weapon against a US city
thinEvidence.note: Iran has no known nuclear weapon, and such an attack would invite devastating retaliation.

thinEvidence.text: Iranian leaders have threatened to wipe Israel off the map
thinEvidence.note: Iranian leaders have repeatedly called for Israel's elimination, though the translation of the 2005 phrase is disputed.

thinEvidence.text: No large-scale amphibious invasion has been attempted since the Korean War
thinEvidence.note: Nothing since has matched Inchon's scale, though smaller opposed landings occurred, such as Cyprus in 1974 and the Falklands in 1982.

thinEvidence.text: A large share of the world's oil and gas exports passes through the Strait of Hormuz
thinEvidence.note: The EIA puts about a fifth of world petroleum liquids and a similar share of LNG trade through the strait.

thinEvidence.text: We are living in the last days foretold in the Bible
thinEvidence.note: A matter of faith with no testable content.

thinEvidence.text: The US no longer keeps tactical nuclear weapons in its arsenal
thinEvidence.note: The US still holds B61 gravity bombs, about a hundred of them deployed in Europe, and fielded the low-yield W76-2 warhead in 2020.

thinEvidence.text: Losing control of TikTok cut China's main channel for influencing American opinion
thinEvidence.note: The US ownership deal reduces one channel, but Chinese influence operations run across many platforms, so calling TikTok the main one overreaches.

thinEvidence.text: Markets and history show a major war follows a period of debt and wealth gaps
thinEvidence.note: Debt and inequality often precede internal turmoil, but historians find no reliable pattern linking them to great-power war; the big cycle rests on a selective reading of a few empires.

thinEvidence.text: Mass-produced autonomous weapons would deter China from invading Taiwan
thinEvidence.note: Untested; deterrence depends on many factors and autonomous mass has not been fielded at scale in the Pacific.

thinEvidence.text: The UN mediates conflicts before they escalate into a world war
thinEvidence.note: UN mediation has helped end some wars, but the Security Council is deadlocked where great powers are involved.

thinEvidence.text: Militaries are removing humans from parts of the targeting decision cycle
thinEvidence.note: US demonstrations and Israeli practice show human steps cut or reduced to supervision, though final strike approval formally stays with humans.

thinEvidence.text: The US military is ahead of China in adopting AI for war
thinEvidence.note: Neither side publishes its assessment, and China's military AI adoption is opaque.

thinEvidence.text: The US military uses AI to find and rank targets in its current wars
thinEvidence.note: Maven Smart System is in wide use for target identification and prioritization, as officials have described publicly.

thinEvidence.text: Missile and drone attacks now outmatch air defences
thinEvidence.note: Mass drone and missile salvos have saturated defences in Ukraine and the Gulf, but defences still intercept most incoming fire in many attacks.

thinEvidence.text: Modern warfare favours the defence over the offence
thinEvidence.note: Ukraine shows defenders using drones and surveillance to stall offensives, but long-range missile and drone strikes still get through air defences.

thinEvidence.text: NATO's Article 5 does not automatically oblige allies to fight
thinEvidence.note: The treaty commits each ally only to such action as it deems necessary, so a military response is a political choice.

thinEvidence.text: NATO cannot yet move forces to its eastern flank fast enough to deter Russia
thinEvidence.note: NATO and the EU acknowledge military-mobility gaps in permits, bridges and rail, though forward-deployed brigades reduce the need for speed.

thinEvidence.text: A new US land-based ICBM is not worth its cost
thinEvidence.note: Whether the Sentinel missile is worth its rising cost is a budget and strategy judgment, not a testable fact.

thinEvidence.text: North Korea's artillery and nuclear weapons deter any attack on it
thinEvidence.note: No state has attacked North Korea since 1953, and studies of a second Korean war project very heavy early losses in Seoul.

thinEvidence.text: North Korea would lose a conventional war with the US and South Korea
thinEvidence.note: US and South Korean forces far outmatch the North's ageing conventional forces, though the North could inflict heavy damage first.

thinEvidence.text: Nostradamus accurately predicted Napoleon and Hitler
thinEvidence.note: 'Hister' is the Latin name of the Danube and the Napoleon anagram needs letter swaps; the matches were fitted after the events.

thinEvidence.text: Nostradamus predicted a third world war
thinEvidence.note: The quatrains are vague verse read after the fact; none names a third world war, its date or its parties, and no reading has forecast a war before it happened.

thinEvidence.text: A nuclear-armed Iran could be managed through deterrence
thinEvidence.note: Deterrence has held with North Korea, but a nuclear Iran could spur regional proliferation and riskier crises.

thinEvidence.text: Nuclear deterrence does not stop limited aggression below the nuclear threshold
thinEvidence.note: The Falklands, the 1973 war, the 1969 Sino-Soviet clashes and Kargil show nuclear-armed states attacked on a limited scale.

thinEvidence.text: Nuclear weapons technology is old enough that any industrial state can build it
thinEvidence.note: The physics and engineering are well known, but producing fissile material in secret remains the main barrier, which is why few states have succeeded.

thinEvidence.text: No one can know the date of the end times from signs like blood moons
thinEvidence.note: A theological position on date-setting.

thinEvidence.text: Only a small minority of Western Europeans would fight to defend their country
thinEvidence.note: Surveys such as Gallup's 2024 poll found only about a quarter or fewer of Germans, Italians and others say they would fight for their country.

thinEvidence.text: People overestimate violence because vivid news reports are easy to recall
thinEvidence.note: The availability bias is well established, but how much of public belief about violence it explains is less measured.

thinEvidence.text: Periods of nuclear tension have historically eased within a few years
thinEvidence.note: The Cuban crisis was followed by the 1963 test ban and the 1983 war scare by the INF treaty, but some rivalries stayed tense for decades.

thinEvidence.text: Pinker overstates prehistoric violent death rates by selecting violent samples
thinEvidence.note: Critics show his samples skew toward violent and post-farming sites, though his defenders note that lower-violence samples have their own gaps.

thinEvidence.text: Predictions of a third world war have recurred continually since 1945
thinEvidence.note: Warnings of an imminent third world war appear in press and official statements from 1945 onward, and none has yet come true.

thinEvidence.text: Prehistoric hunter-gatherers rarely waged war
thinEvidence.note: Paleolithic evidence of warfare is sparse, but sites like Nataruk and Jebel Sahaba show group killing at or before the dawn of farming, and the record is thin both ways.

thinEvidence.text: Preparations such as stockpiles and resilient power could greatly improve Taiwan's ability to withstand a blockade
thinEvidence.note: Modelling shows larger fuel inventories and hardened power extend Taiwan's endurance, though this is untested in practice.

thinEvidence.text: President Trump could be removed from office over the Iran war
thinEvidence.note: Removal needs two-thirds of the Senate and no US president has ever been removed; the base rate is near zero.

thinEvidence.text: Psychic visions can predict when a world war will start
thinEvidence.note: Tests of psychic forecasting find no accuracy above chance, and this source's own timing for the war has already shifted.

thinEvidence.text: Publicly releasing intelligence on Russia's build-up helped Ukraine survive the 2022 invasion
thinEvidence.note: The disclosures undercut Russian false-flag pretexts and rallied allies, but Ukraine's survival owed more to its forces and Russian planning failures.

thinEvidence.text: Recent wars show that modern war bogs down even strong militaries
thinEvidence.note: Ukraine and Gaza became long wars of attrition, but short decisive campaigns such as Azerbaijan's in 2023 still happen.

thinEvidence.text: A renewed war with Iran would collapse the global economy
thinEvidence.note: A Gulf supply shock can push oil far higher and cause recession, but a collapse worse than the 1930s goes well beyond what the 2026 disruption produced.

thinEvidence.text: The return of Jews to Israel fulfils biblical end-times prophecy
thinEvidence.note: Reading modern Israel as a sign of the end times is religious interpretation that no evidence can settle.

thinEvidence.text: Rising gold and silver prices show investors expect a major war
thinEvidence.note: Precious metals rose on central-bank buying, interest rates and currency worries; prices do not single out war.

thinEvidence.text: A rising power becomes most dangerous once it believes it has become strong
thinEvidence.note: Power-transition theory supports the idea, but historians dispute how often rising powers start wars rather than declining ones.

thinEvidence.text: Russia cares more that Americans doubt their elections than about who wins
thinEvidence.note: Undermining trust was a documented aim, but the 2017 US intelligence assessment also found a clear Russian preference for one candidate in 2016.

thinEvidence.text: Russia, China, Iran and Turkey are forming an axis that will dominate the Middle East
thinEvidence.note: Turkey is a NATO member at odds with Iran and Russia in Syria, and the others cooperate loosely without any alliance.

thinEvidence.text: Russia could not surprise NATO with an attack on the Baltic states
thinEvidence.note: A large build-up would be seen, but 2022 showed leaders may disbelieve warning, and a small snap attack would shorten it.

thinEvidence.text: Russia has failed to gain air superiority over Ukraine [2026]
thinEvidence.note: Ukrainian ground-based air defence has kept Russian aircraft largely to stand-off weapons such as glide bombs throughout the war.

thinEvidence.text: Russia and Iran will lead a coalition invasion of Israel
thinEvidence.note: Russia keeps working ties with Israel and has shown no intent to attack it; Iran's strikes have been missile and proxy attacks, not an invasion with Russia.

thinEvidence.text: Russia is likely to break any ceasefire in Ukraine
thinEvidence.note: A forecast of behaviour; Russia broke the Minsk ceasefires, but no general ceasefire has existed to test it.

thinEvidence.text: Russia's military spending matches Europe's when adjusted for purchasing power
thinEvidence.note: IISS-style PPP estimates put Russia near Europe's nominal total, but that compares a PPP figure with a nominal one; Europe's own PPP spending is higher.

thinEvidence.text: Russia's military will shrink once wartime stop-loss is lifted
thinEvidence.note: Many contracts are held only by stop-loss and the force is old, but Moscow could raise conscription or pay to hold numbers.

thinEvidence.text: Russia's war in Ukraine has revived North Korea's economy
thinEvidence.note: Bank of Korea estimates show its fastest growth in years alongside Russian payments, though gains are concentrated in Pyongyang and rebound from a pandemic collapse.

thinEvidence.text: Russia will not stop until it reaches the Danube, the Carpathians, the Vistula and the Baltic
thinEvidence.note: That line runs through NATO territory, and forecasters put a Russian attack on NATO well under even odds; Russia's stated war aims centre on Ukraine.

thinEvidence.text: A Russian armoured attack on the Baltic states or Finland would fail at heavy cost
thinEvidence.note: Against NATO air power it would likely take heavy losses, but wargames such as RAND's show Russia could still reach Baltic capitals quickly.

thinEvidence.text: Sanctions cannot stop North Korea because China keeps trading with it
thinEvidence.note: China accounts for the vast majority of North Korea's trade and has enforced UN sanctions loosely.

thinEvidence.text: The Saudi government will be overthrown within the next two years
thinEvidence.note: The Saudi monarchy has a long record of stability and there is no sign of an imminent revolt.

thinEvidence.text: Semiconductors would not be the main reason for a US-China war over Taiwan
thinEvidence.note: A judgment about the motives of a war that has not happened.

thinEvidence.text: A single high-altitude nuclear blast could knock out the power grid across a large part of the US
thinEvidence.note: A high-altitude burst would cause an electromagnetic pulse that could damage grid equipment over a wide area, but how much would fail and for how long is disputed.

thinEvidence.text: A small nuclear arsenal deters as well as a large one
thinEvidence.note: Minimum deterrence is a strategic judgment about what leaders fear; there is no test of how deterrence varies with arsenal size.

thinEvidence.text: South Korea's shrinking population will erode its military edge over North Korea
thinEvidence.note: South Korea's manpower pool is shrinking fast, but its economic and technological lead over the North remains vast.

thinEvidence.text: States that gave up nuclear weapons programmes were later attacked
thinEvidence.note: Libya and Ukraine were attacked after disarming, but Iraq had no weapons to give up, and South Africa and Kazakhstan were never attacked.

thinEvidence.text: By a strict definition there have been many more than two world wars
thinEvidence.note: Under definitions like Hamilton and Herwig's (five or more major powers, fighting on two or more continents), several 17th- and 18th-century wars qualify.

thinEvidence.text: Strong central states reduce violence by removing the incentive to strike first
thinEvidence.note: Homicide fell as states consolidated and violence clusters in failed states, but correlation in timing is not proof of the mechanism.

thinEvidence.text: Supporting Ukraine now costs Europe less than defending against Russia later
thinEvidence.note: Studies such as the Kiel Institute's put aid to Ukraine at a fraction of the cost of rearming against a victorious Russia, but the estimate rests on assuming Russia would attack.

thinEvidence.text: Taiwan's dependence on imported energy is its main weakness under a blockade
thinEvidence.note: Taiwan imports almost all of its energy and holds only days to weeks of LNG in reserve.

thinEvidence.text: Taiwan makes nearly all of the world's most advanced chips
thinEvidence.note: TSMC produces roughly nine in ten of the world's leading-edge logic chips.

thinEvidence.text: The Taiwan Strait's weather and tides allow an invasion only a few times a year
thinEvidence.note: Monsoons and typhoons leave roughly two favourable windows, in spring and autumn, though they span weeks rather than single days.

thinEvidence.text: Taiwan will come under China's control peacefully as their economies grow together
thinEvidence.note: Polls in Taiwan show support for unification in single digits and a rising Taiwanese identity, so peaceful absorption looks unlikely on current trends.

thinEvidence.text: AI targeting can make errors faster and at greater scale than humans
thinEvidence.note: Automated systems can repeat an error across many targets quickly, but comparative error rates against human targeting are not public.

thinEvidence.text: Today's arms race is the most destructive in human history because it includes AI
thinEvidence.note: The Cold War nuclear build-up to tens of thousands of warheads remains far more destructive than any AI arms race so far.

thinEvidence.text: Today's conflicts resemble the imperial armed peace of small wars before 1914
thinEvidence.note: An interpretive framework for current conflicts, not a checkable fact.

thinEvidence.text: Trade makes people more valuable alive than dead and so reduces war
thinEvidence.note: Commercial-peace studies find a modest effect, but dense trade did not prevent 1914 or Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

thinEvidence.text: Tribal and hunter-gatherer societies had far higher rates of violent death than modern states
thinEvidence.note: Ethnographic and archaeological data show high rates of violent death, though the samples are selective and the size of the gap is disputed.

thinEvidence.text: Trump has put US arms sales to Taiwan on the negotiating table with China [2026]
thinEvidence.note: Based on reported summit readouts and leaks; the substance of the private talks is not public.

thinEvidence.text: Trump's withdrawal from the Iran nuclear deal led Iran to expand its nuclear program
thinEvidence.note: IAEA reports show Iran complied until 2018-19, then enriched to 60% and grew its stockpile after the US withdrawal.

thinEvidence.text: Ukraine's fate after giving up its nuclear weapons will push other countries to seek them
thinEvidence.note: Public support for nuclear weapons has risen in South Korea and elsewhere, but no new state has begun a weapons program.

thinEvidence.text: Ukraine retook more territory than Russia captured [2025]
thinEvidence.note: Open-source trackers such as ISW and DeepState show Russia gaining several thousand square kilometres in 2025 against small Ukrainian recaptures.

thinEvidence.text: The United States will reinstate a military draft because of the war with Iran
thinEvidence.note: Automatic Selective Service registration is not a draft; induction needs a new act of Congress, and none has been proposed.

thinEvidence.text: Using the dollar for sanctions pushes other countries away from holding dollars
thinEvidence.note: Central banks have shifted some reserves into gold since 2022, but the dollar's share of reserves has fallen only slowly.

thinEvidence.text: Using the Iran war to choke China's oil supply would lead to war with China
thinEvidence.note: China has supplied Iran but avoided any military clash with the US during the war, and forecasters see a US-China war as unlikely in the near term.

thinEvidence.text: The US is waging a proxy war against Russia in Ukraine more intense than any Cold War proxy war
thinEvidence.note: Western arms and intelligence support for Ukraine has few Cold War parallels, but Soviet roles in Korea and Vietnam make 'more intense than any' a stretch, and 'proxy war' is a contested label.

thinEvidence.text: War became common only after the rise of farming and settled societies
thinEvidence.note: Signs of warfare rise sharply with settlement and farming in many regions, though some earlier group violence existed.

thinEvidence.text: The war with Iran is the first major US war since 1945 that began without majority public support
thinEvidence.note: Polling on the 2026 war is not independently checkable here; earlier wars such as Iraq in 2003 did start with majority support.

thinEvidence.text: The war with Iran has made a Chinese invasion of Taiwan less likely
thinEvidence.note: Some analysts read the war as a demonstration of US strike power and China's oil exposure; others argue depleted US munitions raise the risk. The net effect is uncertain.

thinEvidence.text: The war in Ukraine will spread to draw in Poland and Belarus
thinEvidence.note: After more than four years neither Poland nor Belarus has joined the fighting despite drone incursions, and forecasters put a direct Russia-NATO war in the next few years well under even odds.

thinEvidence.text: Wars between rising and ruling powers are usually triggered by a third party's provocation
thinEvidence.note: 1914 fits, but many power-transition wars were started directly by one of the rivals.

thinEvidence.text: The wars in Europe and the Middle East could merge with a Taiwan crisis into one world war
thinEvidence.note: A conceivable worst case, but the great powers have so far avoided fighting each other directly in either war.

thinEvidence.text: Wars in Ukraine and the Middle East have depleted US munitions needed to deter China
thinEvidence.note: Pentagon and think-tank reviews show interceptor and long-range munition stocks drawn down faster than they are replaced.

thinEvidence.text: Washington inflates foreign threats to justify defence budgets
thinEvidence.note: A claim about motives behind threat assessments that no measurement settles.

thinEvidence.text: AI weapons reduce civilian casualties by making strikes more precise
thinEvidence.note: Precision weapons have cut collateral damage compared with area bombing, but AI targeting has not been shown to reduce civilian harm and may speed up strikes.

thinEvidence.text: A well-prepared smaller country can deter or defeat a larger invader
thinEvidence.note: Ukraine stopped Russia's drive on Kyiv, but smaller states have often lost to larger invaders, and outcomes depend heavily on outside support.

thinEvidence.text: Western economies will collapse under the energy shock of the war with Iran
thinEvidence.note: Past oil shocks caused recessions, not collapse, and benchmark prices eased during the war.

thinEvidence.text: The US will invade Cuba within the next few years
thinEvidence.note: Pressure, sanctions and an oil blockade are not an invasion, and nothing in the public record points to a planned invasion.

thinEvidence.text: The world today resembles the eve of the First World War
thinEvidence.note: Multipolar rivalry and regional powder kegs echo 1914, but nuclear deterrence and the absence of mobilisation-driven war plans make the analogy loose.

thinEvidence.text: The world today resembles the run-up to the Second World War
thinEvidence.note: A historical analogy, a way of framing events rather than a testable claim.

thinEvidence.text: A world war needs rival blocs with rough military and economic parity
thinEvidence.note: Power-transition research links great wars to narrowing power gaps, but wars have also begun between unequal sides and the US lead over China has narrowed.

thinEvidence.text: World War 3 will be triggered by false-flag attacks staged by globalists
thinEvidence.note: There is no evidence of any plan to stage false flags to start a world war; the claim rests on channelled visions.

thinEvidence.text: The US would not defend the Baltic states under Trump
thinEvidence.note: Whether a US president would honour Article 5 is a question of intent that no public record settles.

thinEvidence.text: China would invade Taiwan to seize its chip factories if it fell far behind in AI
thinEvidence.note: A statement about Chinese leaders' intentions that no public record can show.

thinEvidence.text: War is an innate part of human nature
thinEvidence.note: Humans show a capacity for both coalitional violence and long peace; whether war is innate depends on definitions.
